l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The people of Nephi destroyed the government of the land by murdering the chief judge and dividing into tribes with separate leaders and laws. A secret combination led by Jacob established a wicked band and fled to the northernmost part of the land. Nephi preached repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ, performed miracles, cast out devils, and raised his brother from the dead. Some people were converted, baptized with water, and healed through the power and Spirit of God.

l: the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The people of Nephi destroyed the government of the land, divided into tribes, and turned from the Lord their God. Some were converted through Nephi's ministry, but only a few were converted unto the Lord.

l: chief judge of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The chief judge of the land was murdered on the judgment seat in the thirtieth year.

l: government of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The government of the land was destroyed when the people divided into tribes and when secret combinations undermined its regulations.

l: tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The people separated into tribes according to family, kindred, and friends. The tribes became exceedingly great, established their own laws, and agreed not to go to war one with another.

l: leaders of tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Each tribe appointed a chief or leader over itself. The leaders established the laws and manner of government for their tribes.

l: Satan, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The iniquity among the people came because they yielded themselves unto the power of Satan.

l: secret combination, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The secret combination caused great iniquity and destroyed the regulations of the government. It gathered together under Jacob and fled to the northernmost part of the land.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The prophets testified of Jesus, but the people stoned them, cast them out, and some members of the secret combination murdered prophets.

l: Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Jacob became the king of the wicked band and had given his voice against the prophets who testified of Jesus. He commanded the band to flee to the northernmost part of the land.

l: wicked band, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The wicked band was led by Jacob and was formed by the secret combination. It fled northward to build a kingdom and await dissenters.

l: the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The land was divided among tribes and leaders, and its government was destroyed. Some degree of peace existed in the land despite the people's wickedness.

l: laws, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The tribes were not united in their laws, which were established according to the minds of their chiefs and leaders. They made strict laws against one tribe trespassing against another.

l: Nephi (son of Helaman), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi testified boldly of repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. He ministered with power, cast out devils, raised his brother from the dead, performed many miracles, and ordained men to baptize with water.

l: angels, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Angels had visited Nephi, and they ministered unto him daily because of his great faith on the Lord Jesus Christ.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi preached repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. The converted believed in him, and miracles were performed in his name.

l: Spirit of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The converted testified that they had been visited by the power and Spirit of God. Those healed or delivered from devils manifested that they had been wrought upon by the Spirit of God.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Baptism with water was a witness and testimony before God that people had repented and received a remission of their sins.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi preached repentance and remission of sins. Many were baptized unto repentance in the commencement of the thirty-third year.

l: remission of sins, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi preached remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. Those who repented and were baptized with water received a remission of their sins.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Those brought unto repentance were baptized with water as a witness and testimony before God and the people. Nephi ordained men to perform this ministry.

l: murder of the chief judge, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The chief judge of the land was murdered on the judgment seat in the thirtieth year, contributing to the destruction of the government.

l: division into tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The people divided into tribes according to family, kindred, and friends. Each tribe appointed a leader and established its own laws and manner of government.

l: preaching repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi preached repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. He continued preaching to the people at the commencement of the thirty-third year.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: In the thirty-fourth year, a great storm, tempest, thunder, lightning, and earthquake caused widespread destruction and changed the face of the land. Zarahemla was set on fire, Moroni sank into the sea, and Moronihah was covered by the earth and became a mountain. After about three hours of destruction, thick darkness covered the land for three days, preventing any light or fire. The people mourned, howled, and wept, and some cried that repentance would have spared their brethren, mothers, daughters, and children.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Jesus is named in connection with miracles: no man could perform a miracle in his name unless he was cleansed from his iniquity.

l: the people of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The people looked earnestly for the sign given by prophet Samuel, the Lamanite, but doubtings and disputations arose among them. After the destruction and darkness, they mourned, howled, and wept continually, and some cried that they should have repented.

l: the sign of darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The sign of darkness was given by prophet Samuel, the Lamanite, and concerned darkness covering the land for three days.

l: darkness for three days, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Darkness for three days occurred after the storm and destruction. No light was seen during that time, and the inhabitants who had not fallen could feel the vapor of darkness.

l: the great storm, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The great storm arose in the thirty-fourth year, in the first month, on the fourth day, and was unlike any storm previously known in the land.

l: the great and terrible tempest, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The great and terrible tempest occurred with terrible thunder, exceedingly sharp lightning, and great destruction, shaking the whole earth as if it would divide asunder.

l: Zarahemla, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The city of Zarahemla caught fire during the destruction. The people later cried that their brethren would have been spared if they had repented before the great and terrible day.

l: the city of Moroni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The city of Moroni sank into the depths of the sea, and its inhabitants were drowned.

l: the city of Moronihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The earth was carried up upon the city of Moronihah, and a great mountain occupied the place where the city had been. The people later cried that their mothers, fair daughters, and children would have been spared if they had repented.

l: land northward, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The land northward suffered a more great and terrible destruction than the land southward. Its whole face was changed, highways and level roads were broken or spoiled, cities were sunk, burned, or shaken down, and many inhabitants were slain or carried away in the whirlwind.

l: the great and terrible destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The great and terrible destruction included storms, whirlwinds, thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, fires, sinking cities, fallen buildings, and widespread deaths. It lasted about three hours before darkness covered the land.

l: thick darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Thick darkness covered all the face of the land after the destruction. The inhabitants who had not fallen could feel its vapor, and it prevented candles, torches, and fire from producing light.

l: light, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: There was no light during the darkness: candles, torches, fire, the sun, the moon, and the stars could not be seen or provide light.

l: mourning, howling, and weeping, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Mourning, howling, and weeping occurred continually among the people during the three days of darkness because of the darkness and the great destruction.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Some people cried that if they had repented before the great and terrible day, their brethren, mothers, fair daughters, and children would have been spared.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: This unit concerns the inhabitants of the earth, the destruction of many cities and people because of wickedness, and a call for those spared to repent and return to Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ declares that he created the heavens and the earth, fulfills the law of Moses, and offers eternal life, mercy, redemption, and salvation from sin. He teaches that sacrifices and burnt offerings are ended and that a broken heart and a contrite spirit are required. He also teaches that those who come to him as little children may enter the kingdom of God, and that believers may receive baptism with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Many people and cities are destroyed because of wickedness, abominations, secret murders, combinations, and rejection of prophets. Those who are spared are called to return to Jesus Christ, repent, and be converted.

l: the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The earth is the place where a voice is heard among all inhabitants, where many destructions occur, and where Jesus Christ says he created the heavens and the earth.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Prophets are cast out and stoned by wicked inhabitants. The blood of the prophets cries against those responsible, and many people are destroyed because they rejected the prophets.

l: the saints, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The blood of the saints cries against wicked people, and destructions are caused so that their blood will not come any more against them.

l: destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Many great destructions come upon the land and the people because of their wickedness and abominations. Cities are burned, sunk, covered with earth, or buried.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The inhabitants who are spared are called to repent of their sins and return to Jesus Christ. Those who repent and come unto him may have eternal life and be saved.

l: conversion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The spared inhabitants are called to be converted. The Lamanites are described as having been converted through faith in Jesus Christ and baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ identifies himself as the Son of God, the creator of the heavens and the earth, the light and life of the world, and Alpha and Omega. He offers mercy, eternal life, redemption, and salvation from sin, and calls people to repent and come unto him.

l: the Son of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The kingdom of God is mentioned in connection with those who come unto Jesus Christ as little children.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ says that he was with the Father from the beginning, that he is in the Father and the Father is in him, and that the Father has glorified his name in him.

l: the coming of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The scriptures concerning the coming of Jesus Christ are fulfilled. He says that he came unto his own, but his own received him not.

l: sons of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ gives those who receive him the opportunity to become the sons of God, and he will do the same for those who believe on his name.

l: redemption, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Redemption comes by Jesus Christ, and he says that he came into the world to bring redemption unto the world.

l: sacrifices, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ commands that the shedding of blood, sacrifices, and burnt offerings no longer be offered to him because he will accept none of them.

l: broken heart, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ accepts a broken heart as a sacrifice. Whoever comes to him with a broken heart will be baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: contrite spirit, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ accepts a contrite spirit as a sacrifice. Whoever comes to him with a contrite spirit will be baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Those who come to Jesus Christ with a broken heart and a contrite spirit will be baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost. The Lamanites experienced this baptism at the time of their conversion, though they knew it not.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The Holy Ghost is received with fire by those who come to Jesus Christ with a broken heart and a contrite spirit. The Lamanites were baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost because of their faith in Jesus Christ.

l: sin, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The people are urged to repent of their sins, and Jesus Christ says that he came to save the world from sin.

l: kingdom of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The kingdom of God is for those who come unto Jesus Christ as little children.

l: childlike followers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Those who repent and come unto Jesus Christ as a little child will be received by him. Jesus Christ says that the kingdom of God belongs to such people.

l: death of Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ says that he laid down his life for those who come unto him as little children.

l: resurrection of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ says that he laid down his life and took it up again.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The people of the land hear a voice calling the house of Israel to repent and return, and warning that their dwellings will become desolate if they do not. After three days of darkness, trembling, destruction, mourning, and silence, the land is restored and the spared people turn their mourning into joy and praise to the Lord Jesus Christ, their Redeemer. The more righteous people are spared because they received the prophets and did not shed the blood of the saints. In the thirty-fourth year, Christ manifests himself to the people of Nephi who were spared and to the Lamanites who had been spared, showing them his body and ministering to them.

l: the people of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They hear and witness the sayings and the voice. After hearing the voice, they weep and howl again because of the loss of their kindred and friends.

l: Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: He testified concerning a remnant of the seed of Joseph.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It is addressed as a people whom the Lord has gathered and nourished, but who would not be gathered. The spared house of Israel is told that it will be gathered if it repents and returns with full purpose of heart; otherwise, its dwellings will become desolate until the covenant to its fathers is fulfilled.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: He is the one whose praise and thanksgiving the spared people offer after their mourning is turned into joy. After his ascension into heaven, he manifests himself to the spared people of Nephi and the spared Lamanites.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: He is identified as the Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, whom the spared people praise and thank.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They are among those to whom Christ manifests himself after his ascension into heaven. He shows them his body and ministers to them.

l: the Lamanites who had been spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They are among those to whom Christ manifests himself after his ascension into heaven. He shows them his body and ministers to them.

l: the remnant of the seed of Joseph, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Jacob testified concerning it, and the text identifies the people being addressed as a remnant of its seed.

l: Lehi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: He brought the plates of brass out of Jerusalem.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The more righteous part of the people received them and did not stone them. Many testified of the events at the coming of Christ and were slain because they testified.

l: the promised land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It is silent for many hours after the people hear the sayings and the voice. It later experiences darkness, trembling, rending rocks, groanings, tumultuous noises, and destruction, after which the earth stands again.

l: the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It trembles, and its rocks rend during the three days. It later ceases trembling, cleaves together again, and stands.

l: the voice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It speaks again to all the people after a period of silence. It asks the house of Israel how often it would have gathered them and calls them to repent and return.

l: the plates of brass, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They are said to have been fulfilled by the events. Whoever reads them is told to search them and see whether the destructions fulfill the prophecies of the holy prophets.

l: the covenant to their fathers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Its fulfilling is identified as the time until which the dwellings of the house of Israel may remain desolate.

l: the prophecies, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: The prophecies of many holy prophets concern the deaths and destructions by fire, smoke, tempests, whirlwinds, and the opening of the earth.

l: the deaths and destructions, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They occur through fire, smoke, tempests, whirlwinds, and the opening of the earth to receive people. The text says they fulfill the prophecies of many holy prophets.

l: the coming of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Many testified of these things at the coming of Christ, and they were slain because they testified.

l: the ascension of Christ into heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: After it, Christ manifests himself to the people of Nephi who were spared and to the Lamanites who had been spared.

l: the ministry of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It includes Christ showing his body to the spared people and ministering to them. An account of this ministry is to be given later.

l: darkness for three days, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They pass away while the land experiences darkness, trembling, destruction, and tumultuous noises. In the morning after them, the darkness and disturbances cease.

l: thick darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It covers the face of the land during the three days. In the morning, it disperses.

l: the mourning, weeping, and wailing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: They are made by the people who are spared alive and cease after the earth stands again. Their mourning is turned into joy, and their lamentations into praise and thanksgiving.

l: silence, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: It remains in all the land for many hours because the people are astonished after hearing the sayings. The people later hear the voice again.

l: the blessing and favors shown to the spared people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Great favors are shown and great blessings are poured upon the heads of the spared people of Nephi and the spared Lamanites. Soon afterward, Christ manifests himself to them, shows them his body, and ministers to them.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: A great multitude of the people of Nephi gathers around the temple in the land Bountiful and hears the Father testify of his Beloved Son. Jesus Christ appears, declares that he is the light and life of the world, and lets the multitude feel the wounds from his crucifixion. He gives Nephi and others power to baptize, specifies the baptismal words and method, and declares his doctrine of repentance, belief, baptism, and becoming as a little child. He teaches that contention is of the devil and that those who build on his doctrine build on his rock and can inherit the kingdom of God.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The great multitude gathers around the temple in the land Bountiful, marveling at the great change and conversing about Jesus Christ. They hear the Father's voice, see Jesus Christ descend from heaven, feel the prints of the nails in his hands and feet and the wound in his side, worship him, and receive his doctrine.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ appears to the great multitude, identifies himself as the one whom the prophets testified would come, and declares that he is the light and life of the world. He gives Nephi and others power to baptize, teaches his doctrine, and warns against adding to or taking away from it.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The Father speaks from heaven and commands the people to hear his Beloved Son, in whom he is well pleased and through whom he has glorified his name. The Father gives the doctrine to Jesus Christ, bears record of him, commands all men everywhere to repent and believe in him, and is one with Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The Holy Ghost bears record of the Father and Jesus Christ. The Holy Ghost is one with the Father and Jesus Christ and visits those who believe in Jesus Christ with fire.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Nephi is among the multitude and comes forth when Jesus Christ commands him. Jesus Christ gives Nephi power to baptize the people.

l: death of Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The people converse about Jesus Christ's death, concerning which a sign had been given. Jesus Christ says that he has been slain for the sins of the world and permits the people to witness the wounds from his death.

l: the sins of the world, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ says that he has taken upon himself the sins of the world and suffered the will of the Father in all things from the beginning.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ gives Nephi and others power to baptize those who repent through their words and desire to be baptized in his name. Baptism is performed in the water in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, by immersing the person and bringing the person forth from the water.

l: doctrine of Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: The doctrine of Jesus Christ is that all people should repent and believe in him, be baptized, become as a little child, and thereby receive salvation and the kingdom of God. Jesus Christ teaches that no more or less should be declared as his doctrine, and that it is a rock against which the gates of hell shall not prevail.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ commands all men everywhere to repent and teaches that those who repent through the words of those with authority and desire baptism may be baptized. He also commands people to repent and become as a little child.

l: belief in Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ teaches that the Father commands all men everywhere to believe in him. Those who believe in him and are baptized shall be saved, and those who believe in him also believe in the Father.

l: contention, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ teaches that the spirit of contention is not of him but is of the devil, who stirs up the hearts of people to contend with anger. He declares that stirring up anger against one another is not his doctrine and that such things should be done away.

l: little child, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ teaches that people must become as a little child, repent, and be baptized in his name or they cannot receive these things or inherit the kingdom of God.

l: kingdom of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 11
s: Those who believe in Jesus Christ and are baptized shall be saved and shall inherit the kingdom of God. Jesus Christ teaches that those who repent, are baptized in his name, and become as a little child can inherit it.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus teaches Nephi, the twelve, and the multitude about baptism, repentance, humility, righteousness, mercy, purity, peacemaking, and enduring persecution. He appoints twelve to minister and baptize with water, while he baptizes believers with fire and the Holy Ghost. Jesus explains that he fulfills the law and commandments and teaches reconciliation, purity of heart, truthful communication, nonresistance, generosity, love for enemies, and perfection. He tells the people to let their light shine, remain the salt of the earth, and keep his commandments to enter the kingdom of heaven.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus gives the twelve power and authority to baptize with water and says that he will baptize believers with fire and the Holy Ghost. He teaches the multitude to repent, come unto him with a broken heart and contrite spirit, keep his commandments, love their enemies, and be perfect.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The twelve are chosen from among the people to minister to them and be their servants. They receive power and authority to baptize with water, and those who believe their testimony and are baptized may receive fire, the Holy Ghost, and a remission of sins.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The Holy Ghost is received by those who believe, come down into the depths of humility, and are baptized. Those who hunger and thirst after righteousness shall be filled with the Holy Ghost.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: God is the Father in heaven, and people are to glorify him through their good works. He makes his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and the pure in heart shall see him.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The kingdom of heaven belongs to the poor in spirit who come unto Jesus and to those who are persecuted for his name’s sake. Those who do not keep Jesus’s commandments cannot enter into it.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The people are taught to heed the words of the twelve, believe in Jesus, repent, be baptized, reconcile with others, and let their light shine through good works. They are also told to love their enemies, bless those who curse them, and pray for those who use and persecute them.

l: the law of Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus says that he did not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them. The law is fulfilled in him, and old things are done away while all things become new.

l: the commandments, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus gives the people the commandments of his Father, including believing in him, repenting, coming unto him with a broken heart and contrite spirit, and keeping his commandments. Keeping them is required to enter the kingdom of heaven.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The twelve baptize believers with water, and Jesus baptizes them with fire and the Holy Ghost. Those who believe, humble themselves, and are baptized receive a remission of their sins.

l: sin, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Those who are baptized after coming down into the depths of humility shall receive a remission of their sins. Jesus teaches that lustful looking is adultery in the heart and commands that such things not enter the heart.

l: the gospel teachings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: The teachings in this unit call for humility, repentance, mercy, purity in heart, peacemaking, reconciliation, truthful speech, generosity, love of enemies, and prayer for persecutors. They teach that good works should lead people to glorify the Father in heaven.

l: the salt of the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus gives the people to be the salt of the earth. If the salt loses its savor, it is good for nothing and is cast out to be trodden under foot of men.

l: the light of this people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Jesus gives the people to be the light of this people. He teaches that a city set on a hill cannot be hid and that their light should shine so others may see their good works and glorify their Father in heaven.

l: persecution, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 12
s: Those who are persecuted for Jesus’s name’s sake are blessed, and theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Jesus says they should have great joy and be exceedingly glad because their reward in heaven is great.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Jesus teaches about almsgiving, prayer, fasting, forgiveness, treasures, light, and serving God rather than Mammon. He instructs that the heavenly Father sees acts done in secret and rewards them openly, and that forgiveness from the Father depends on forgiving others. Jesus tells the twelve to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness and not to worry about food, drink, or clothing. He teaches that the heavenly Father knows their needs and will provide for them, while each day has sufficient trouble of its own.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Jesus teaches that alms, prayer, and fasting should not be done to be seen by men. He tells the twelve to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness and not to take thought for their lives.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The heavenly Father sees what is done in secret and rewards it openly. He knows what people need, feeds the fowls of the air, and clothes the grass of the field.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Prayer should be offered in secret to the Father, without vain repetitions or much speaking. Jesus gives a manner of prayer that asks for the Father's name to be hallowed, his will to be done, forgiveness, and deliverance from evil.

l: heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Heaven is where the Father's will is done. Treasures laid up in heaven are not corrupted by moth or rust and are not stolen by thieves.

l: kingdom of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The kingdom of God is to be sought first, along with his righteousness. Jesus teaches that other needed things will be added to those who seek it first.

l: treasures, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Earthly treasures can be corrupted by moth and rust and stolen by thieves. Treasures should instead be laid up in heaven, because where a person's treasure is, there will the person's heart be also.

l: earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Earth is where the Father's will is to be done as it is in heaven. Treasures on earth are vulnerable to corruption and theft.

l: light, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The light of the body is the eye. If the eye is single, the whole body is full of light; if the eye is evil, the body is full of darkness.

l: Mammon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Mammon is a master that cannot be served together with God. A person will hate one master and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: The twelve are the people Jesus chose to minister unto this people. Jesus tells them to remember his words and not to take thought for food, drink, or clothing.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: This people is the group whom Jesus chose the twelve to minister unto.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 13
s: Jesus warns that those who worry about clothing and provision may be of little faith. He teaches that the heavenly Father will clothe them if they are not of little faith.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Jesus teaches the multitude not to judge hypocritically, to ask, seek, and knock, and to treat others as they would want to be treated. He contrasts the strait gate and narrow way leading to life with the broad way leading to destruction, and warns against false prophets by their fruits. Jesus teaches that not everyone who calls him Lord will enter the kingdom of heaven, but those who do the will of his Father. He compares those who hear and do his sayings to a wise man whose house stands on rock, and those who hear but do not do them to a foolish man whose house falls on sand.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Jesus teaches the multitude to judge not, to ask, seek, and knock, and to do to others as they would have others do to them. He warns against false prophets and teaches that those who hear and do his sayings are like a wise man who built his house upon a rock.

l: judgment, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Judgment is measured back to people according to the judgment and measure they use. Jesus teaches that people should first remove the beam from their own eye before seeking to remove the mote from another’s eye.

l: asking, seeking, and knocking, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Asking, seeking, and knocking are associated with receiving, finding, and having the way opened. Jesus teaches that the Father gives good things to them that ask him.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The Father is in heaven and gives good things to them that ask him. Jesus identifies doing the will of the Father as the condition for entering the kingdom of heaven.

l: men, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Men are taught to do to others what they would want others to do to them.

l: the law and the prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The law and the prophets are identified with the teaching that men should do to others as they would want others to do to them.

l: golden rule, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The golden rule is stated as doing to men whatever one would want men to do to oneself.

l: strait gate, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The strait gate is the entrance associated with the narrow way that leads unto life. Few find it.

l: broad way, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The broad way is wide and leads to destruction. Many enter through it.

l: destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Destruction is the destination of the broad way, which has a wide gate and many who enter it.

l: life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Life is the destination of the narrow way entered through the strait gate. Few find the way that leads unto life.

l: false prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: False prophets come in sheep’s clothing but are inwardly ravening wolves. They are recognized by their fruits.

l: fruits, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Fruits reveal what kind of tree produces them and allow people to know false prophets. Good fruit comes from a good tree, while evil fruit comes from a corrupt tree.

l: good tree, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: A good tree brings forth good fruit and cannot bring forth evil fruit.

l: corrupt tree, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: A corrupt tree brings forth evil fruit and cannot bring forth good fruit. Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Not everyone who says, Lord, Lord, enters the kingdom of heaven. The one who enters is the person who does the will of the Father in heaven.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: Those who say they prophesied, cast out devils, and did wonderful works in Jesus’s name may still be told to depart because they work iniquity.

l: house, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: A house built upon a rock withstands rain, floods, and winds, while a house built upon sand falls when those forces beat upon it.

l: rock, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The rock is the foundation of the house built by the wise man. The house does not fall because it is founded upon the rock.

l: sand, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The sand is the foundation of the house built by the foolish man. The house falls when rain, floods, and winds beat upon it.

l: fall of the house, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 14
s: The fall of the house occurs when the foolish man’s house, built upon sand, is beaten by rain, floods, and winds. Its fall is described as great.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Jesus teaches the multitude that the law given through Moses is fulfilled in him, while prophecies and the covenant concerning things to come are not destroyed. He commands the twelve disciples, who are a light to a remnant of the house of Joseph, to keep his commandments and endure to the end. Jesus explains that the Father has other sheep among separated tribes who will hear his voice and become one fold with one shepherd. He also teaches that the Gentiles will be converted through the preaching of the twelve but will not hear his voice directly except through the Holy Ghost.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Jesus teaches that the law given unto Moses is fulfilled in him and that he is the law and the light. He commands his disciples to keep his commandments, identifies them as his sheep, and says he will give eternal life to those who endure to the end.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Father gave Jesus commandments concerning the twelve disciples, the other tribes of the house of Israel, and the other sheep. The Father separated peoples because of iniquity and gave the twelve disciples to Jesus.

l: the law of Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The law given unto Moses is fulfilled in Jesus and has an end in him. Jesus says he does not destroy the prophets or the things that are yet to come.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Jesus tells the twelve disciples that they are his disciples and a light unto the people who are a remnant of the house of Joseph. He says they have heard his voice and seen him, and commands them to keep his commandments.

l: the house of Joseph, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: A remnant of the house of Joseph is the people among whom the twelve disciples are a light. The Father gave their land of inheritance to them.

l: the other tribes of the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The Father led the other tribes of the house of Israel away out of the land and separated them from the people because of their iniquity. They do not know of the twelve disciples.

l: the other sheep, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The other sheep are not of the fold of the twelve disciples, but Jesus must bring them and they will hear his voice. The twelve disciples are identified as these other sheep.

l: the fold, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The fold is understood by the disciples as referring to their group, but Jesus teaches that other sheep are not of this fold and will also be brought into one fold.

l: the shepherd, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Jesus teaches that there shall be one fold and one shepherd.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: The disciples misunderstood Jesus and supposed that the other sheep were the Gentiles. Jesus explains that the Gentiles should be converted through the preaching of the disciples and should not hear his voice directly except through the Holy Ghost.

l: life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Jesus promises eternal life to those who endure to the end.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 15
s: Iniquity caused the separation of the twelve disciples and the other tribes from others and caused them not to know of one another.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Jesus says that he has other sheep in lands outside Jerusalem who have not yet heard his voice, and that he will go to them so there may be one fold and one shepherd. He commands that his sayings be written so the people at Jerusalem and other tribes may gain knowledge through the Holy Ghost, and so the Gentiles may bring the remnant of the house of Israel to knowledge of him. The Father will gather the house of Israel from the earth and fulfill his covenant, while the Gentiles are blessed for belief but warned that rejecting the fulness of the gospel will cause it to be taken from them. The Father commands that this land be given to this people as an inheritance, and Isaiah’s words concerning Jerusalem and Zion will be fulfilled.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Jesus says that he has other sheep outside the land of Jerusalem and that he will go to them so they may hear his voice and be numbered among his sheep. He commands that his sayings be written and teaches about the gathering of the house of Israel, the Gentiles, the gospel, and the fulfillment of the Father’s covenant.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Father commands Jesus to go to other sheep, promises to bring the fulness of the gospel to the house of Israel, and will remember his covenant with them. He blesses believing Gentiles, warns unbelieving Gentiles, and commands that this land be given to this people as an inheritance.

l: Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: Jerusalem is identified as a land where Jesus has ministered and as the place whose people have seen and been with him. Its waste places will break forth into joy when the Lord comforts his people and redeems Jerusalem.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The house of Israel is described as having unbelief, being scattered, smitten, afflicted, slain, cast out, hated, and made a hiss and a byword among the Gentiles. The Father will remember his covenant with them, bring the gospel to them, gather them from the four quarters of the earth, and bring them to knowledge of the fulness of the gospel.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Gentiles are blessed because of their belief in Jesus and the Holy Ghost, and the truth and fulness of these things will come to them because of the unbelief of the house of Israel. They are warned that if they reject the fulness of the gospel and commit various sins, the Father will bring the fulness of his gospel from among them; if they repent and return, they will be numbered among the house of Israel.

l: other sheep, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The other sheep are not of the land of Jerusalem or the surrounding lands where Jesus has ministered. They have not yet heard his voice or seen him, but Jesus will go to them so they can hear his voice and be numbered among his sheep.

l: the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The earth is the place upon whose face the remnant of the seed of the house of Israel will be scattered because of unbelief. The Father will gather them from the four quarters of the earth, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of God.

l: the promised land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Father commands Jesus to give this land to this people for their inheritance.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The fulness of the gospel will be manifested unto the Gentiles and brought to the house of Israel. If the Gentiles sin against it and reject its fulness, the Father will bring the fulness of the gospel from among them; if they repent and return, they will be numbered among the house of Israel.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The Father has made a covenant with all the people of the house of Israel. He will remember and fulfill that covenant by gathering them and bringing them to knowledge of the fulness of the gospel.

l: knowledge of Jesus and the gospel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The written sayings are to help the people at Jerusalem and other tribes receive knowledge through the Holy Ghost. The remnant of the house of Israel may be brought to a knowledge of Jesus, and the house of Israel will come to knowledge of the fulness of the gospel.

l: Jesus's voice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 16
s: The other sheep have not yet heard Jesus’s voice, but Jesus will go to them so they shall hear it. Those who hear and are numbered among his sheep will be part of one fold with one shepherd.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus tells the multitude to return to their homes, ponder his words, ask the Father for understanding, and prepare for the next day. He heals all the sick and afflicted people brought to him, and the multitude worships him. Jesus prays to the Father for the multitude and blesses their little children, while angels descend and minister to the children. The multitude witnesses these events and bears record of them.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus tells the multitude to go home, ponder his words, ask the Father for understanding, and prepare their minds for the next day. He heals the sick and afflicted people, prays to the Father, blesses the little children, weeps, and tells the multitude to behold their little ones.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The Father is the one Jesus says he is commanded by to speak. Jesus goes unto the Father and prays unto him for the multitude and their little children.

l: the multitude, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The multitude listens to Jesus, brings the sick and afflicted people and the little children to him, worships him, and bears record of his prayer and the angels ministering to the children. It numbers about two thousand five hundred souls and consists of men, women, and children.

l: the sick and afflicted people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The sick and afflicted people are brought to Jesus, including those who are lame, blind, halt, maimed, leprous, withered, deaf, dumb, or afflicted in any manner. Jesus heals every one of them as they are brought forth.

l: the little children, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The little children are brought and set down around Jesus. Jesus takes them one by one, blesses them, and prays for them, while angels descend and minister unto them.

l: angels, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The angels descend out of heaven as it were in the midst of fire. They encircle the little children about and minister unto them.

l: healing the afflicted, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus invites the sick and afflicted people to come to him because he has compassion and mercy. He heals every one of them as they are brought forth.

l: Jesus's prayer to the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus kneels upon the earth and prays unto the Father, but the things he prays cannot be written. The multitude bears record that they heard great and marvelous things and felt joy as he prayed for them.

l: the children's blessing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus takes the little children one by one, blesses them, and prays unto the Father for them. Afterward, he tells the multitude to behold their little ones as angels descend and minister unto them.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: Jesus says that the multitude's faith is sufficient for him to heal them. He tells the multitude that they are blessed because of their faith.

l: joy, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 17
s: The multitude is filled with joy while Jesus prays for them and is overcome after he finishes praying. Jesus says that his joy is full, and he weeps.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus teaches the disciples and the multitude how to administer and receive bread and wine in remembrance of his body and blood. He commands them to pray, meet together, welcome and minister to others, keep his commandments, and avoid temptation and disputation. Jesus gives the disciples power to give the Holy Ghost, then departs from the multitude and ascends into heaven.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus commands the disciples and the multitude concerning bread, wine, prayer, worship, repentance, baptism, and his commandments. He touches the chosen disciples, gives them power to give the Holy Ghost, and ascends into heaven.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The disciples bring bread and wine, administer them to the multitude, and are commanded to continue doing so in remembrance of Jesus. Jesus touches them and gives them power to give the Holy Ghost, and they bear record that he ascended into heaven.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The multitude sits, eats bread, drinks wine, and hears Jesus teach them to pray, meet together, welcome others, and hold up their light. They do not hear the words Jesus speaks while he touches the disciples.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The Father receives the disciples' testimony that they remember Jesus and are willing to obey his commandments. Jesus teaches the people to pray to the Father in his name.

l: the people of Jesus's church, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The people who repent and are baptized in Jesus's name are to receive the bread and wine and meet together. They are to pray for others and avoid disputations.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus's church is to administer bread and wine to those who believe and are baptized in his name. Prayer is to occur in the church among people who repent and are baptized in his name.

l: the devil, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The devil may tempt people and lead them away captive. Jesus commands the people to watch and pray so they will not be led away by him.

l: Satan, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Satan desires to have the people and sift them as wheat. Jesus commands them always to watch and pray so they will not enter into temptation.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The disciples receive power to give the Holy Ghost after Jesus touches them one by one.

l: heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus departs from the multitude and ascends into heaven, and the disciples see and bear record of it.

l: bread, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus takes bread, breaks and blesses it, gives it to the disciples, and commands them to eat and give it to the multitude. Bread is administered in remembrance of Jesus's body.

l: wine, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus commands the disciples to drink wine from the cup and give it to the multitude. Wine is administered in remembrance of Jesus's blood.

l: Jesus's body, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus commands the people to eat bread in remembrance of his body, which he has shown to them.

l: blood of Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus commands the people to drink wine in remembrance of his blood, which he has shed for them.

l: Jesus's flesh, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus teaches that those who knowingly eat his flesh unworthily eat damnation to their souls. Those known to be unworthy are to be forbidden from partaking, while still being ministered to and prayed for.

l: Jesus's Spirit, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus teaches that those who always remember him will have his Spirit with them.

l: the light of this people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus says that he is the light and commands the people to hold up their light to the world by following what they have seen him do.

l: the gospel sacrament, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: The text describes bread and wine being broken, blessed, eaten, and drunk in remembrance of Jesus's body and blood, and commands this practice to continue.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus commands the people to watch and pray always, pray to the Father in his name, pray in their families, and pray for those who come to worship with them.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Those who repent and are baptized in Jesus's name may receive the flesh and blood. People who do not repent are not numbered among Jesus's people, though others should continue to minister to them.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Those who believe and are baptized in Jesus's name are to receive the bread and wine. A person who repents and is baptized may be received and ministered to.

l: temptation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus warns that the devil and Satan can lead people into temptation. He commands the people to watch and pray always and warns that disobeying his commandment can lead to temptation.

l: the commandments, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus gives commandments concerning the sacrament, prayer, worship, ministering, worthiness, and avoiding disputations. Those who keep them are blessed and built upon his rock.

l: the Holy Ghost ordination, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: Jesus touches the chosen disciples one by one and gives them power to give the Holy Ghost.

l: the ascension of Christ into heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 18
s: After touching the disciples, Jesus is covered by a cloud, departs from the multitude, and ascends into heaven. The disciples see and bear record of his ascension.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: After Jesus ascends into heaven, the multitude gathers again, and the twelve disciples teach them, pray, and baptize those Jesus had chosen. The Holy Ghost falls upon the baptized disciples with fire, angels minister to them, and Jesus comes to minister unto them. Jesus prays to the Father for the disciples and for those who will believe on their words, asking that they may receive the Holy Ghost, be purified, and be one with him and the Father. The disciples continue praying to Jesus, and Jesus says that he has never seen such great faith among all the Jews.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Jesus ascends into heaven, later returns to minister unto the disciples, and commands the multitude and disciples to kneel and pray. He prays to the Father for the Holy Ghost, for believers, and for the purification and unity of his disciples and those who believe on their words.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: The Father is prayed to by the multitude, the disciples, and Jesus in the name of Jesus. Jesus thanks the Father for giving the Holy Ghost to those he chose and asks that believers receive the Holy Ghost and be purified.

l: the multitude, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: The multitude disperses after Jesus ascends, then gathers again after hearing that Jesus will show himself. It is divided into twelve bodies, taught by the disciples, led to kneel and pray, follows the disciples to the water, witnesses the Holy Ghost and fire, and hears and understands the words of Jesus's prayer in their hearts.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: The disciples teach the multitude, pray, and minister unto the people. They are baptized, receive the Holy Ghost and fire, are ministered to by angels and Jesus, become white as Jesus, and continue praying steadfastly unto him.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Nephi is among the twelve disciples chosen by Jesus. He goes down into the water, is baptized, and then baptizes all those whom Jesus had chosen.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: The Holy Ghost is desired by the disciples and is given to them after they are baptized. It falls upon them with fire, and Jesus prays that it will also be given to all who believe on the disciples' words.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: The multitude and the disciples pray to the Father in the name of Jesus, and the disciples pray to Jesus as their Lord and their God. Jesus also prays to the Father, while the disciples continue praying to Jesus without ceasing and with great desire.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Nephi is baptized in the water and then baptizes all those whom Jesus had chosen. After they are all baptized and come out of the water, the Holy Ghost falls upon them.

l: Jesus's ministering, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Jesus ministers unto the disciples after angels minister to them. He also teaches the multitude, commands them and the disciples to pray, blesses the disciples, and speaks of the great things they have seen and heard.

l: belief in Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Jesus says that he chose the disciples because of their belief in him. He asks the Father to give the Holy Ghost to those who will believe in the disciples' words because they believe in Jesus.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Jesus thanks the Father for purifying those he chose because of their faith. He says that he has never seen such great faith among all the Jews and prays that those who believe on the disciples' words may be purified through faith.

l: purification, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 19
s: Jesus says that the disciples have been purified because of their faith. He prays that those who believe on the disciples' words may also be purified in him and that he may be glorified in them.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jesus Christ gives the multitude and the disciples bread and wine, and the multitude is filled with the Spirit and gives glory to him. He teaches that the words of Isaiah will be fulfilled, the covenant of the Father with the house of Israel will be fulfilled, and the remnants of Israel will be gathered and brought to the knowledge of the Lord their God. He declares that the Gentiles will be blessed through the Holy Ghost but will face judgment if they harden their hearts after receiving the fulness of the gospel. He prophesies the establishment of the house of Israel in a New Jerusalem, the redemption and reinhabiting of Jerusalem, and the fulfillment of the covenant made with the Father’s people.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jesus Christ commands the multitude and the disciples to pray in their hearts, gives them bread and wine, and teaches that they are his body and blood to the soul. He declares that the words of Isaiah, the covenant with the house of Israel, the gathering of Israel, and the redemption of Jerusalem will be fulfilled.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The Father commands Jesus Christ to give the land as an inheritance and to finish the commandment concerning the house of Israel. The Father makes covenants with his people, will gather them, will establish them in the land, and will bring judgment upon the nations of the Gentiles if they do not repent.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The multitude is commanded to arise, receives bread and wine, eats and drinks, and is filled with the Spirit. The multitude cries out with one voice and gives glory to Jesus Christ.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The disciples are commanded to pray in their hearts, arise, eat bread, and drink wine. They are also commanded to break bread and give it, and to give wine, to the multitude.

l: house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The house of Israel is the people concerning whom Jesus Christ finishes the Father’s commandment. Its remnants will be gathered from the earth, brought to the knowledge of the Lord their God, established in a New Jerusalem, and blessed through the fulfillment of the covenant.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The Gentiles receive a blessing through the pouring out of the Holy Ghost and become mighty above all, unto the scattering of the house of Israel. If they do not repent after receiving the blessing and scattering the people, or if they harden their hearts after receiving the fulness of the gospel, their iniquities will return upon their own heads.

l: the remnant of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The remnant of the house of Jacob will go forth among the Gentiles and be among them as a lion among beasts and as a young lion among flocks of sheep. Its hand will be lifted up upon its adversaries, and its enemies will be cut off.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The prophets, from Samuel and those who follow after, have testified of Jesus Christ. The people are described as children of the prophets and of the covenant made with their fathers.

l: Abraham, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Abraham received the covenant that in his seed all the kindreds of the earth would be blessed. The Father fulfills this covenant through the blessing of the people and the pouring out of the Holy Ghost through Jesus Christ upon the Gentiles.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The remnants of Israel will be brought to the knowledge of the Lord their God, who has redeemed them.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The Holy Ghost is poured out through Jesus Christ upon the Gentiles as a blessing. This blessing makes the Gentiles mighty above all, unto the scattering of the people of the house of Israel.

l: Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jerusalem will be given to the gathered people as the land of their inheritance and will be inhabited again by them. Jerusalem will be comforted, redeemed, and clothed in beautiful garments as the holy city.

l: New Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The Father will establish the people in the land, and it will be a New Jerusalem. The powers of heaven will be in the midst of this people, and Jesus Christ will be in their midst.

l: the promised land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The promised land is identified as the land of Jerusalem and is described as the land of inheritance for the people forever.

l: bread, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jesus Christ breaks and blesses bread, gives it to the disciples, and commands the disciples to give it to the multitude. He teaches that whoever eats this bread eats of his body to the soul.

l: wine, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jesus Christ gives wine to the disciples and commands them to give it to the multitude. He teaches that whoever drinks this wine drinks of his blood to the soul.

l: the sacrament of bread and wine, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The bread and wine are given and consumed by the disciples and the multitude. Jesus Christ teaches that the bread is his body and the wine is his blood to the soul, and those who eat and drink shall never hunger or thirst but shall be filled.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The covenant made by the Father with the house of Israel will be fulfilled when the words of Isaiah are fulfilled. The Father will remember the covenant, gather his people in his own due time, and give them again the land of their fathers for their inheritance.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: When the Gentiles have received the fulness of the gospel, they may still harden their hearts against Jesus Christ. If they do, the Father will return their iniquities upon their own heads.

l: the scattering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The Gentiles receive a blessing through the Holy Ghost that makes them mighty above all, unto the scattering of the people of the house of Israel. They are also described as a scourge unto the people of the land.

l: gathering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: The remnants of Israel will be gathered from the east, west, south, and north and brought to the knowledge of the Lord their God. The Father will gather his people together again and give them Jerusalem for the land of their inheritance.

l: salvation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 20
s: Jerusalem will be redeemed without money, and the people will know the name of Jesus Christ. The people will announce peace and salvation, and Jerusalem will be inhabited again with the people as the land of their inheritance.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: Jesus Christ declares that the Father will gather the dispersed house of Israel, establish Zion, and fulfill the covenant through works brought forth from the Gentiles. The Gentiles will be tested by whether they repent, accept Jesus Christ’s words, and are numbered among the house of Israel. The remnant of Jacob will receive power, assist in gathering Israel, and build the New Jerusalem, where the power of heaven will come down. The Father’s work and gospel will extend among the dispersed people and all nations, while those who refuse to repent will be cut off.
